reviews.title: misleading and a disappointing waste of time!
reviews.text:
I downloaded this app after seeing and ad claiming that you should enter any topic or issue and instantly find relevant Quran verses or Hadith related,

Instead, i was forced to go through an unnecessary long and frustrating personal questionnaire, only to discover that its actually a paid app for prayer, Quran, and Hadith reminders.

So far, I haven’t find the feature that was advertised in the first place.

This is completely misleading and a disappointing waste of time. SHAME ON YOU GUYS.

reviews.title: can’t even use the app
reviews.text: i’ve used plethora of Islamic apps over the year, but this one takes the cake. When you download the app, you can’t even use it without having to commit to a seven-day free trial. There is no hidden X in the corner anywhere , no way to back out of the subscription page. I love the widget that they have for the lock screen, but you can’t click on it to take it to the app to read more because the ENTIRE APPLICATION is hidden behind a paywall. The greed is getting too much, to force people to commit to any subscription, just use the app is wrong on so many levels, even if there is a seven-day free trial, or I read another comment where it said you can get a free membership but even still, that’s messed up. I hate to leave such a negative comment/review. It makes me feel bad, but the app is unusable without having to subscribe to any type of service. And I will not be doing that. This app seem like a good idea, but it’s made by people who are too greedy you’re supposed to want to support the Ummah. Not feel forced to. I can’t even go onto the app and think about subscribing after seeing all the benefits no, you have to subscribe to use any part of the app. This is how you turn away Muslims, old and new. Please fix it and please heed my words inshallah, there will be some change

reviews.title: Disappointing and Misleading Subscription
reviews.text: I downloaded this app hoping to strengthen my faith and learn more about Islam, but I was disappointed to be asked to pay for a subscription after completing the sign-up process. This should have been made clear from the beginning. I understand developers need to earn money, but I don’t believe an app meant to bring people closer to Allah should put essential religious guidance behind a paywall. Islamic knowledge should be accessible to everyone.

reviews.title: Pay for faith
reviews.text: I’ll be the first one to say that I am not strong with my faith nor have I been strong with it for a very long time. Though I would never imagine that making almost a minimum of $320,000 a year off of the subscriptions of 10,000 users is justified. An Imam would never make such money in a year, to teach and help strengthen faith is their job.

reviews.title: The Qur’an Is Divine Guidance, Not a Subscription Business.
reviews.text:
There is something deeply uncomfortable about turning access to the words of Allah into a recurring subscription business.

The Qur’an was revealed as guidance for humanity, not as a commercial product.

I have no objection to developers being fairly compensated for their work, technology, maintenance and innovation. But there is a fundamental difference between charging for a service that helps people engage with the Qur’an and exploiting their desire to remain connected to Allah.

That distinction matters.
Making Qur’anic reminders accessible should be an act of service, not merely another opportunity to maximise subscription revenue.

The Qur’an is priceless. Our responsibility is to ensure that access to its guidance does not become a privilege reserved for those who can afford to pay.
